summary: DONE is correct, landed in #710 (60633eff3), which the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3 also contains. Shell snapshots, getProjectShellById and the shell stream's project-upserted items now read repository_identity_json from projection_projects (migration 086), so there are no git spawns on the snapshot path. ProviderCommandReactor.start uses a targeted pending-goal SQL query. A background sync (startup, a 30-minute sweep, project.created and root/kind moves) skips chats and missing roots. It probes git in the background lane only when a stat-based fingerprint of <commonDir>/config changes or the entry is older than 24 h. Neither of the finding's costs remains: the 250-380 ms of boot probing and the up-to-1 s snapshot wait. I found no other first-party hot path that still spawns identity git. The remaining resolver callers are the background sync, AgentControlProjectPlans (one root per plan), and the enrichment for the legacy replayEvents/replayEventsPage RPC, which no first-party client calls. The fix has two small defects. (1) A transient probe failure is stored as 'no repository' for up to 24 h, survives restarts, and is announced to clients. (2) Remote changes that Ryco makes itself, such as publishRepository, only appear at the next 30-minute sweep.

evidence.note: buildShell is pure SQL: 'repository identities are persisted ... so a snapshot never waits on git'. Identity is decoded from row.repositoryIdentityJson at :2646, :3129, :3227, :3267, :3364 and :3384. resolveRepositoryIdentitiesForProjects and the RepositoryIdentityResolver import are gone (git show f1be4abc7 had them at :529/:560/:2183/:2658/:2806/:2837).

toShellStreamEvent maps project.created, project.meta-updated and project.avatar-set to getProjectShellById, which reads the persisted identity. This is the main client stream path, and it spawns no git.

start() calls readPendingGoalSyncThreads. The live implementation at ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3279 uses listPendingGoalSyncThreadRows (:928): goal_json IS NOT NULL plus a json_valid-guarded json_extract(...)='pending'.

syncProject skips chats and missing roots (null fingerprint) and returns 'fresh' when the fingerprint is unchanged and checkedAt is under 24 h old. Otherwise it calls resolver.refresh in inBackgroundProcessLane and records the result.
repository-identities.sync runs after commandGate.signalCommandReady (:1028). runRepositoryIdentitySync forkScopes both the event consumer and the sweep, so it does not block boot.
The projector upsert keeps the identity columns while workspace_root is unchanged and clears them on a move. recordRepositoryIdentity (:161) is guarded by project_id AND workspace_root.

DEFECT SOURCE: makeGitIdentityProbe turns every failure into null, whether a timeout (1 s, :97/:126), a spawn error or a non-zero exit. A transient failure is therefore indistinguishable from 'not a repository / no remote'.

DEFECT: that null is recorded with the current fingerprint and checkedAt (:119-125). Later sweeps treat it as 'fresh' (:108-114) for 24 h, even across restarts, because the state is persisted. If a non-null identity was stored before, samePersistedRepositoryIdentity is false and the empty project.meta.update (:133) announces the removal to every client.

publishRepository adds a remote through git.ensureRemote, and GitVcsDriver initRepository runs git init. Neither triggers an identity resync. Nothing revalidates on read or on git activity, so the new identity appears only at the next 30-minute sweep (repositoryIdentitySync.ts:43). Before the fix, a snapshot or reconnect after the 1-minute TTL picked it up.

enrichProjectEvent is only reached from the legacy replayEvents/replayEventsPage RPCs (orchestrationRpc.ts:473/:500), which no first-party client calls. A persisted null is ambiguous, so project.created replays for chats, non-repo projects and deleted projects still call resolver.resolve. This path is not hot, and it was already this way before the fix.
The tests cover fingerprint gating, max-age, chat/missing/deleted skips, the moved-root guard, non-blocking event consumption and trigger selection. No test covers a refresh failure or timeout.

fixDefects: (1) A transient probe failure becomes a sticky 'no repository' state. RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts:128-135 collapses a timeout (over 1 s of process runtime), a spawn error or a non-zero exit into null. repositoryIdentitySync.ts:115-125 then persists that null with the current fingerprint and checkedAt, and :108-114 treats it as fresh for 24 h. The state is persisted, so a server restart does not clear it. If a real identity was stored before, :127-146 dispatches project.meta.update, so every client drops the project's repository grouping, remote link and hero metadata. The old code cached such a miss for 1 minute only. This is most plausible on Windows (slow spawns under Defender) or a heavily loaded machine. The first sweep after upgrade runs right after boot. (2) Remote changes made by Ryco itself go stale. publishRepository (SourceControlRepositoryService.ts:507-525, via ensureRemote) and initRepository change <commonDir>/config, but no sync is triggered. The identity updates only at the next 30-minute sweep, where before a reload after 1 minute picked it up. (3) Minor. A newly created git project first streams with a null identity, then a second upsert arrives once the sync records and announces it. This causes a brief regroup and an extra project.meta-updated event per new repository project, and after upgrade one such event per git project on the first sweep. Not done from the optional proposal step: still 2 spawns per root (rev-parse plus remote -v) instead of parsing config. That now only runs in the background, so it is negligible.
implementationSketch: (1) Separate 'indeterminate' from 'no identity'. In apps/server/src/project/Layers/RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts, make the probe return a tagged result, e.g. {ok: stdout} | {exit: code} | {failed: cause}. Keep resolve() collapsing everything to null for interactive callers. Change refresh() to fail with a typed RepositoryIdentityProbeError when either probe times out or cannot spawn, and do not Cache.set in that case. Update RepositoryIdentityResolverShape['refresh'] in project/Services/RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts. In repositoryIdentitySync.ts syncProject, catch that error and return 'skipped' without calling recordRepositoryIdentity. The old identity, fingerprint and checkedAt then stay as they were, so the next sweep (or an earlier short retry, e.g. a 1-2 minute Schedule just for failed roots) tries again. Tests: in repositoryIdentitySync.test.ts, inject a resolver whose refresh fails. Assert that record and dispatch are not called and that a later sync with a working resolver records the identity. In RepositoryIdentityResolver.test.ts, assert that a VcsProcess timeout makes refresh fail while resolve still returns null. (2) Expose the sync as a small service, e.g. RepositoryIdentitySync with revalidateRoot(cwd), built in serverRuntimeStartup next to runRepositoryIdentitySync. revalidateRoot enqueues the projects whose workspaceRoot equals or is inside the repository root. Since it is fingerprint-gated, it costs a few stats when nothing changed. Call it after publishRepository, initRepository and ensureRemote. Alternatively hook it into VcsStatusBroadcaster.refreshStatus(cwd) behind a short debounce, which also catches CLI remote edits made through agents. Test: after a mocked publish, the project's persisted identity updates and one project.meta.update is dispatched. (3) Optional. In repositoryIdentitySync.ts, for a project.created trigger, resolve before the projector's first upsert is streamed, or have toShellStreamEvent hold project.created until the sync records it. This is low value and can be skipped.
decisionReason: Internal server change (repository identity resolver and sync). It does not touch auth, E2EE, the hosted lifecycle, the Hub protocol or deploys.
